A Letter

Dear Sir Basser,

I never imagined that a classroom — an Applied Economics class, of all places — would be where I'd find a second father. But that's exactly what happened. From the very first day you stepped in front of us, I already felt something different about you. You weren't just teaching lessons. You were showing us how to live.

Beyond the subject, beyond the track, you saw me. Not just as a student, not just as an athlete — but as a person. You cared for me the way a parent cares for their own child, and that kind of love is rare. You've been there through the Intramurals, through the sweat and adrenaline of the Provincial Meet, and even now as I prepare for the Regional Meet — even when it's no longer your official duty as my coach — you're still here. Still cheering. Still guiding.

That means more to me than any trophy or medal ever could.

You became one of my biggest role models — not because you're perfect, but because you're real. You showed up. Every single time. And that consistency, that genuine care, shaped who I am today and who I'm still becoming.

As I walk into this next chapter, I carry every lesson you've taught me — in the classroom, on the field, and in life. I am who I am, in part, because of you.

Thank you, Sir Basser. From the very bottom of my heart. 🤍

With all the gratitude and love

With love, Jian

Our Journey

Moments I'll
Never Forget

The Beginning

Applied Economics Class

It started inside a classroom. I didn't know then that my Economics teacher would become so much more than that — a mentor, a role model, a second father who'd walk with me far beyond the four walls of school.

The Fire 🔥

Intramurals

The first time I truly felt your support on the field. You showed up — not because you had to, but because that's just who you are. You had our backs before we even knew we needed someone in our corner.

The Victory 🥇

Provincial Meet

Medals. Certificates. Yellow jerseys. But above all, you. The Provincial Meet showed me what it means to have a coach who pours his heart into his athletes — win or lose. You made us believe we could.

Still Here 🌟

Regional Meet — Even Now

You're not my official coach anymore. But you never stopped being my Coach Basser. As I step into the Regional Meet, I run with your words in my head and your belief in my heart. That's the greatest gift you could ever give me.

Everything,
Sir Basser.

Graduating doesn't mean goodbye — it means I carry everything you've given me into wherever life takes me next. Every stride I run, every lesson I apply, every time I push through when it gets hard — that's you. That's your coaching. That's your love showing up.
